messages:
Aisha (PM): Quick sync — we need to lock acceptance buckets for the next catalog onboarding. I sketched 3 buckets: fast-path (lightbench, <50ms p95, soft pin), validated (full bench, <120ms p95, pin), gated (customer-only, enterprise SLA). Thoughts?
Tom (Eng): quick q — how strict is the <50ms? for multi-tenant endpoints that feels tight if we keep larger context.
Ravi (ML): fast-path should be for small-context stateless models only. For any >512 token seq we should default to validated. Bench numbers: fast-path = 50ms p95; validated = 120ms p95; gated = 250ms p95+ with contractual SLA.
Clara (CustomerOps): customers asking for pin windows and migration grace. We need explicit grace periods per bucket. Proposal: fast-path = 30d TTL, validated = 90d, gated = negotiated.
Leo (Product): +1 on grace windows. Also define quality gate: validated must pass our 100-sample eval with no >5% regression on intent tests.
Aisha (PM): Good. Let's codify acceptance criteria list: performance, quality, compatibility (tensor shapes/ops), memory footprint. If any fail, model goes to "canary shim" for rollback.
Tom (Eng): Implementation note: for pinning, we need a per-tenant override flag. Ops team: can we automate temporary pin extensions for migrations? @ops-bot
ops-bot: @Tom (Eng) reported — automation for pin-extension exists as a 1-click runbook, requires SRE approval above 7d.
Ravi (ML): For validated gate, add embedding/semantic stability: embedding drift < 0.03 cos-dist on heldout. Otherwise customer-facing features may break.
Clara (CustomerOps): Customers will push back on <90d for validated. Could we offer a migrate-assist program to reduce friction? (discounted compute + engineer hours)
Leo (Product): Good idea. Program = migration credit + compatibility audit. We'll need a cost estimate.
Tom (Eng): On deprecation: propose soft-deprecation window: announce 60d before stop-serving to fast-path + validated; gated customers get 120d + migration playbook. Also add auto-fallback policy: route to closest compatible variant.
Aisha (PM): Decision points we need today: 1) bucket definitions (ok?) 2) pin TTL defaults (set?) 3) acceptance gate metrics (finalize list) 4) migration incentives (budget?)
Ravi (ML): Metrics list (proposal): - perf p50/p95, - eval regression score (intent F1), - embedding drift, - memory footprint, - ops-compat (quantized run pass).
Clara (CustomerOps): Pin TTL defaults: fast-path 30d, validated 90d, gated negotiated. Migration incentives: suggest 10% credit + 4 hours SE support for early cohorts.
Tom (Eng): Technical constraints: rollback shim adds ~10-15% tail latency if we keep compatibility layers. Need to call out cost impact in the acceptance doc.
Leo (Product): I'll add a line item in roadmap for "compatibility shims" and estimate 2 sprints to ship the audit+playbook flow.
Aisha (PM): Ok, next steps: Leo to update roadmap & budget. Ravi to write the eval checklist. Tom to draft runbook for pin overrides & rollback shim perf impact. Clara to draft migration offer copy for customers. I'll consolidate into an acceptance spec draft by EOD Friday.
Tom (Eng): FYI — small snippet for runbook we can reuse:
```
# pin-extension playbook
1) customer requests via ticket
2) run automated compatibility check
3) SRE review (if >7d extension)
4) grant pin & schedule migration audit
```
Ravi (ML): I'll include an automated scoring snippet for embedding drift in the checklist.
Clara (CustomerOps): I'll pre-write the migration email + FAQ so sales can start early outreach.
Leo (Product): If we agree, can we gate #1 of the roadmap milestone on having this acceptance spec merged? Vote? :thumbsup: = merge this week
Aisha (PM): :thumbsup: from me.
Tom (Eng): :thumbsup:
Ravi (ML): :thumbsup:
Clara (CustomerOps): :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Logged action items: acceptance-spec-draft assigned to Aisha (due 2026-06-12).
